title: Queen Heleni's sukkah
discussedAt: Not discussed in Derech Tevunos; labelled from the markers of chs. 9-10
about: The other half of chapter 10. `bk-83b-ayin` ships the ascribed difficulty, which Ramchal names in the text; this is the ascribed proof, which he does not, so it is labelled from its markers as `bava-metzia-yeush` is. Having both is what shows that the two composites fail in opposite directions: R. Yehudah's evidence is an incident he reports, so there are two things to attack — whether it happened as told, and whether what happened proves the rule — and the Sages go at the second while granting the first entirely.

`משם ראיה?` in the fourth sentence is a trap worth naming. The same three words are a different construct in Ramchal: at Heb p137 / Eng p138–142 `משם ראיה` is the rebuttal that takes the source an opponent brought and turns it into a proof for one's own side, which is the icon `rebuttal-proves-my-point`. Here they are a rhetorical denial — *is there proof from there?* — so the badge is `ground-does-not-reach` and his icon is deliberately absent.
Text: Vilna, as Sefaria's William Davidson edition prints it. The first sentence is the mishnah at 2a; the rest is the baraita quoted at 2b and the Gemara's reading of it.

units.speaker: Mishnah
units.short: over twenty cubits: invalid, and R. Yehudah's dissent
units.he: סוכה שהיא גבוהה למעלה מעשרים אמה – פסולה. ורבי יהודה מכשיר
units.en: A sukkah more than twenty cubits high is invalid; R. Yehudah validates it.

anatomy.note: The rule is a measure, and every sentence after this one is about whether that measure is the right one. Twenty cubits is the aspect the whole dispute turns on.

units.speaker: R. Yehudah
units.short: R. Yehudah: valid up to forty or fifty cubits
units.he: רבי יהודה מכשיר עד ארבעים וחמשים אמה
units.en: A baraita puts a number on the dissent: R. Yehudah validates up to forty or fifty cubits.

anatomy.note: The same aspect as the mishnah, given a bound the mishnah left open.

units.speaker: R. Yehudah
units.short: the elders said nothing about Heleni's high sukkah
units.he: אמר רבי יהודה: מעשה בהילני המלכה בלוד שהיתה סוכתה גבוהה מעשרים אמה, והיו זקנים נכנסין ויוצאין לשם ולא אמרו לה דבר
units.en: R. Yehudah said: it happened that Queen Heleni's sukkah in Lod was more than twenty cubits high, and the elders went in and out of it and said nothing to her.

anatomy.note: One sentence doing two jobs: it reports an incident, and the report is the evidence. Which is why there are two things a challenger may attack — whether it happened as told, and whether what happened proves the rule — and the Sages take only the second.
The premise is unstated and is what the proof really rests on: elders who see an invalid sukkah say so. Their silence is therefore a ruling.

move.reportedOf: the elders who went in and out in Lod

units.speaker: Chachamim
units.short: no proof: a woman is exempt anyway
units.he: אמרו לו: משם ראיה? אשה היתה ופטורה מן הסוכה
units.en: They said to him: is there proof from there? She was a woman, and women are exempt from the sukkah.

anatomy.note: The incident is granted in full. What is denied is that it reaches the rule: the elders' silence proves nothing where nobody was obligated in the first place. Ramchal's `אחיו הוא במצוות` pattern (Eng p132–136).
The silence concerns a woman's sukkah and the rule concerns a valid sukkah — not the same respect.

units.note: `משם ראיה?` is a question here, and it means the opposite of Ramchal's stock phrase of the same words. His `משם ראיה` (Heb p137) takes the opponent's own source and turns it into a proof for one's own side; this asks whether the source proves anything at all. Different construct, so the icon for his is not used.

units.speaker: R. Yehudah
units.short: she had seven sons, who are obligated
units.he: אמר להן: והלא שבעה בנים הוו לה
units.en: He said to them: did she not have seven sons?

anatomy.note: Seven, and the number is load-bearing: the Gemara will lean on it below to rule out that every one of them was too young.

units.note: It refutes the rebuttal rather than merely weakening it: the premise the Sages relied on — that nobody using the sukkah was obligated — is shown false.

units.speaker: R. Yehudah
units.short: and she acted only on the Sages' word
units.he: ועוד: כל מעשיה לא עשתה אלא על פי חכמים
units.en: And furthermore, she did nothing except in accordance with the Sages.
units.note: A second and independent refutation of the same rebuttal, which is why the Gemara can ask what the first one left undone.

units.short: why was the second answer needed?
units.he: למה לי למיתני ״ועוד כל מעשיה לא עשתה אלא על פי חכמים״?
units.en: Why teach 'and furthermore, she did nothing except in accordance with the Sages'?

anatomy.note: An objection to the report in its parts, in Ramchal's `הא תו למה לי` family: the seven sons had already answered the Sages, so the clause after them adds nothing. The two sentences that follow show it does.

units.short: of seven, one was old enough
units.he: הכי קאמר להו: כי תאמרו בנים קטנים היו, וקטנים פטורין מן הסוכה – כיון דשבעה הוו, אי אפשר דלא הוי בהו חד שאינו צריך לאמו
units.en: This is what he said to them: if you say the sons were minors, and minors are exempt — since there were seven, it cannot be that not one of them was old enough to manage without his mother.

anatomy.note: `כי תאמרו`: the clause is there to shut out a view one might have held — that they were all minors. Ramchal's answer to `פשיטא`, in its `מהו דתימא` form.
Seven does the work: no claim is made about any particular son, only that a count that high cannot be all infants.

units.short: and that is what the second answer is for
units.he: וכי תימרו קטן שאינו צריך לאמו מדרבנן הוא דמיחייב, ואיהי בדרבנן לא משגחה – תא שמע: ועוד, כל מעשיה לא עשתה אלא על פי חכמים
units.en: And if you say that such a minor is obligated only by rabbinic law, and she would not have been scrupulous about rabbinic law — come and hear: and furthermore, she did nothing except in accordance with the Sages.

anatomy.note: `וכי תימרו`: a second view to shut out, one step further back than the first. The clause the objection called idle is the answer to it, so it was not idle.

units.note: The two settlements are one continuous answer in the text, taken in two stages; both are recorded against the objection rather than one against the other, because each closes a different worry.
